texts.value: Key enzyme in myo-inositol biosynthesis pathway that catalyzes the conversion of glucose 6-phosphate to 1-myo-inositol 1-phosphate in a NAD-dependent manner (PubMed:15024000, PubMed:23902760). Rate-limiting enzyme in the synthesis of all inositol-containing compounds (PubMed:15024000)
Inhibited by mood-stabilizing drugs such as valproate (VPA) and lithium
Polyol metabolism; myo-inositol biosynthesis; myo-inositol from D-glucose 6-phosphate: step 1/2
Highly expressed in testis, ovary, heart, placenta and pancreas. Weakly expressed in blood leukocyte, thymus, skeletal muscle and colon
By glucose and lovastain. Up-regulation is prevented by mevalonic acid, farnesol, and geranylgeraniol. Up-regulated by E2F1
Phosphorylation at Ser-279 and Ser-357 may be associated with a decrease in activity
Belongs to the myo-inositol 1-phosphate synthase family
